name: pdf-card-mcp
description: Convert local PDFs into standalone card-based HTML readers, validate notes/highlights, and publish static annotated reader bundles.
long_description: PDF Card Reader is a local-first MCP tool for turning dense PDFs into minimal HTML readers inspired by the source document. It keeps deterministic conversion local, renders source pages, crops detected tables, figures, and formulas as images, derives safe reader styling from the PDF palette, and writes a standalone HTML file that can be moved across devices. Readers support local notes/highlights as a separate sidecar, and the MCP server can validate annotation sidecars or publish static annotated reader bundles. Optional sampling asks the host LLM for validated style-token choices or boundary-only card polish operations without raw CSS or source-text rewrites.

tools.name: convert_pdf_to_card_html
tools.description: Convert a local PDF into a standalone card-based HTML reader with PDF-inspired styling and embedded source-page, table, figure, and formula images. Set style_engine='sampling' for validated host-selected style tokens or postprocess_engine='sampling' for validated card boundary polish.

tools.name: validate_reader_annotations
tools.description: Validate a notes/highlights annotation sidecar against a generated reader HTML file.

tools.name: publish_reader_bundle
tools.description: Publish a generated reader as a single static HTML file or directory bundle with selected public notes and highlights.
